headline: Advance the required-character pointer only on a match
statement: Return whether s is a subsequence of t: every character of s must appear in t in the same order, though other characters may occur between them.
intuition: Match each required character as early as possible in t. An earlier match leaves at least as much suffix for the remaining characters as any later match could.
approach: Point matched at the next character required from s.
Scan t once and advance matched only when its current character is found.
Accept when matched equals the length of s, including an empty s.
correctness: After every scanned prefix of t, matched is the largest prefix length of s that can fit there. A matching character increases that length by one; a nonmatch cannot satisfy the next requirement. The greedy earliest choice preserves every possible remaining suffix, so reaching len(s) is equivalent to subsequence existence.
bruteForce: Enumerate choices of len(s) indices in t and compare their characters.

complexity.explanation: One counter is updated during a single scan of t.

pitfalls: An empty s is always a subsequence.
Repeated letters need separate matching positions.
Do not reset the source pointer after a nonmatch.
